title: delegation-record/1
description: One record per agent hand-off (or its acceptance) from the harness/fixture side (the delegation fixtures, DESIGN.md 7; the delegation study's scenario classes S1-S8). Sibling of dispatch-record/1 sharing the identity fields. The record says WHO handed WHAT to WHOM, through WHICH channel, on WHICH machine — and, through the parent pointer, which earlier hand-off caused this one (the chain the study's tracing-back metric walks).
$comment: Added with the delegation study (0.3.0). The records come from the harness adapter / fixture side (the side that originates the delegation), never from the control: controls stay workload-blind (DESIGN.md 5). Emitted as delegation-records.jsonl on the replay staging volume (the storage that outlives the parent process — the study's outlives-parent scenario reads it after the parent exits). outcome-shaped keys are rejected by the validation-time reject list in framework/records.py (reconciler-only).

stream_id.$comment: DESIGN.md 4: per-slot stream (the emitting adapter/fixture instance).

ts.$comment: DESIGN.md 4: RFC3339 ms; never an ordering key (seq is).

event.$comment: sent = the hand-off record (the giver's side); accepted = the acceptance event (the receiver took the work; sent and accepted are different facts — the study's edge-vs-effect questions hinge on the gap).

channel.$comment: The hand-off's channel class (the study's S1-S5 boundary classes): inproc = a role switch inside one process (S1); child = a child process on the same machine (S2); tool = an agent hiding inside a tool (S3 local, S4 remote); network = agent-to-agent over the network (S5).

delegation_id.$comment: THIS hand-off's identity: opaque, generated by the giver, travels with the task (the study's traveling record — the thing block 4 measures). A delegation_id is born at one 'sent' record and echoed by the receiver's records.

parent_delegation_id.$comment: The hand-off that CAUSED this one (the chain's came-from pointer). Null only at a root (the original request).

root_delegation_id.$comment: The root of the chain (the original request's delegation_id); survives the whole chain so deep hops need no walking.

hop.$comment: 1 = handed directly from the root; 2 = one hand-off in between; ...

from_actor.$comment: The giver: a role or agent instance name (e.g. 'role-A', 'pi-root').

to_actor.$comment: The receiver when known at send time (a child's role, the tool's inner agent); null when the receiver is only known at acceptance (the acceptance event names it).

task_digest.$comment: A digest of the handed task (hashed where sensitive; no payloads).

protocol.$comment: The transport the hand-off itself crossed.

machine.$comment: The which-machine label: which machine this record was written on. Results from different machines are never pooled into one number.

carrier.$comment: How the delegation_id travelled with the task (DESIGN.md 5 carrier vocabulary, extended): mcp_meta | http_header | env | queue_payload | inproc_state | none. 'none' is the study's control condition (block 4 measures what tracing back loses without it).

actor_pid.$comment: The giver's process id at the time of the hand-off (host-side), for process-tree joins.

evidence.$comment: DESIGN.md 4 vocabulary: [{kind, locator}] — where this record came from (the adapter stream line, the queue entry).
